title: QVal: Evaluating Dense Supervision Signals for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
abstract: arXiv:2606.32034v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: LLM agents increasingly act over long horizons, where outcome-only rewards say little about which intermediate actions were good. Dense supervision methods address this by scoring intermediate steps, but they are usually evaluated through the downstream performance of a full training pipeline. This is expensive, confounds signal quality with other training choices, and means that methods are rarely compared on common ground. We introduce QVal, a training-free testbed that measures the $Q$-alignment of a dense signal: whether it orders the candidate actions in each state the same way as their returns under a reference policy do. We benchmark 21 methods from seven families with six open-weight backbones in four environments. Simple prompting baselines are the most $Q$-aligned on average, and performance clusters strongly by family. translated_title: QVal：评估长程LLM智能体的密集监督信号
translated_abstract: LLM智能体越来越多地在长时程任务中执行行动，而仅基于结果的奖励几乎无法说明哪些中间动作是好的。密集监督方法通过为中间步骤打分来解决这一问题，但这类方法通常通过完整训练流程的下游性能来评估。这种方式成本高昂，将信号质量与其他训练选择混为一谈，也意味着这些方法很少在共同基准上进行比较。我们提出了QVal，一个无需训练的测试平台，用于衡量密集信号的$Q$-对齐性：即该信号在每个状态下对候选动作的排序是否与其在参考策略下的回报排序一致。我们在四个环境中，使用六个开源权重骨干模型，对来自七个方法族的21种方法进行了基准测试。结果表明，简单的提示基线平均而言$Q$-对齐性最高，且性能按方法族高度聚集。代码生成的信号仅在小状态和动作空间中表现良好；基于嵌入的信号则……
tldr: 该论文提出QVal——一个无需训练的测试平台，通过衡量密集监督信号在每个状态下对候选动作的排序与参考策略回报排序的一致性（Q-对齐性）来直接评估信号质量，并在四个环境中对七个方法族的21种方法进行基准测试，发现简单提示基线平均Q-对齐性最高且性能按方法族高度聚集。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces QVal, a training-free testbed that evaluates dense supervision signals by measuring their Q-alignment—whether they order candidate actions in each state consistently with their returns under a reference policy—benchmarking 21 methods from seven families across four environments and finding that simple prompting baselines are the most Q-aligned on average.
